title: Reply: only faith-and-salvation necessities were written — Antichrist's hour is not one
source_text: XVIII. Respondeo primo, nos non dicere omnia & singula quae dixit Apostolus scripto mandata esse, sed duntaxat omnia quae necessaria sunt ad fidem & salutem. Hujus generis nihil ab Apostolo viva voce traditum & praedicatum fuit quod in sacris literis scriptum non reperiatur. At dicere nolumus Apostolum non communicasse cum quibusdam singulares quasdam revelationes, quae ad communem totius Ecclesiae salutem non spectant, quae quidem revelationes postea scriptae non fuerint. Quod si Paulus habuit ex peculiari revelatione quando venturus erat Antichristus, illudque docuit Thessalonicenses, certe hoc non ad prius illud genus, sed ad posterius pertinet. Nec enim, puto, dicent ipsi Pontificii rem esse quae sit ad salutem necessaria scire tempus & horam adventus Antichristi.
pass_a_gloss: I answer first that we do not say that all and each things which the Apostle said were committed to writing, but only all things which are necessary to faith and salvation. Of this kind nothing was delivered and preached by the Apostle by living voice which is not found written in the sacred letters. But we do not wish to say that the Apostle did not communicate to certain persons certain singular revelations which do not pertain to the common salvation of the whole Church, which revelations indeed may not afterward have been written. But if Paul had from a peculiar revelation when the Antichrist was to come, and taught that to the Thessalonians, certainly this belongs not to the former kind, but to the latter. For I do not think the Pontificians themselves will say it is a thing necessary to salvation to know the time and hour of the coming of the Antichrist.
pass_b_english: We never claimed every apostolic sentence is in the canon — only all needful to faith and salvation.
Nothing of that saving kind stayed oral-only.
Private revelations to some need not bind the whole church or reach parchment.
Antichrist's clock, if Paul knew it, is that private kind — Rome will not call the hour salvific.
